annotations.description: Choosing to be on the play with this hand is debatable. The hand has no turn-1 play (Breeding Pool could come in untapped but there's nothing to cast for 1 mana with the available colors), and the curve starts at 3 with Formidable Speaker. Being on the draw would give an extra card, which helps find early action and land drops for this slow hand with expensive spells (Deceit at 6, Overlord at 5, Wistfulness at 5). However, being on the play is conventionally correct in most Standard formats to maintain tempo advantage, and this hand does have a reasonable curve into turn 3 Formidable Speaker into turn 4-5 threats. The decision is defensible but worth noting given the hand composition.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to be on the play
annotations.betterLine: Being on the draw could have been considered given the slow hand with no 1-drop and multiple 5+ mana spells, gaining an extra card to smooth out the game plan

annotations.description: Playing Cavern of Souls on turn 2 is suboptimal when the hand contains South Pole Voyager (1W) and Earthen Ally (G) that want colored mana. Cavern of Souls only produces colored mana for one chosen creature type. Floodfarm Verge would provide both W and U (with a Plains/Island condition that could be met later), but more importantly, Starting Town enters untapped on turns 1-3 and produces any color of mana for 1 life. Playing Starting Town now guarantees the ability to cast South Pole Voyager (needing W) on turn 2 alongside Floodfarm Verge or another land on turn 3. With Cavern of Souls, the player can only get colored mana for one creature type (likely Ally), which helps cast Ally creatures but is more restrictive. Starting Town is strictly better here since it enters untapped (turn 2) and produces any color, giving maximum flexibility for the diverse mana requirements in hand (W for Voyager, G for Earthen Ally, B for Boiling Rock Rioter).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Cavern of Souls as the turn 2 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Starting Town (enters untapped on turn 2, taps for any color at 1 life cost), then cast Earthen Ally with G from Starting Town this turn, setting up South Pole Voyager on turn 3 with Floodfarm Verge.

annotations.description: Cavern of Souls requires choosing a creature type. The hand contains South Pole Voyager (Human Scout Ally), Earthen Ally (Human Soldier Ally), and Boiling Rock Rioter (Human Rogue Ally). Choosing 'Human' would make all three castable with uncounterable colored mana. Choosing 'Ally' would also cover all three. 'Warrior' matches none of the creatures currently in hand, meaning the Cavern will only produce colorless mana for any creature the player actually wants to cast soon.
annotations.actionTaken: Named 'Warrior' for Cavern of Souls
annotations.betterLine: Name 'Human' or 'Ally' to enable colored mana for South Pole Voyager, Earthen Ally, and Boiling Rock Rioter — all creatures currently in hand.

annotations.description: Playing Earthen Ally (a creature) before combat when the player has Allies at Last (a combat trick) in hand is suboptimal sequencing. However, the more pressing issue is land sequencing: the player has Cavern of Souls as their only land and multiple lands in hand (Floodfarm Verge, Starting Town, Breeding Pool, Starting Town). They should play a land first to have mana available for future turns. Playing Earthen Ally for G requires a green source - Cavern of Souls can produce colored mana only for the chosen creature type, so if Ally was chosen, this works. But the player should play a land drop first (this is their main phase, and they need to make a land drop). They're casting Earthen Ally using Cavern of Souls, but they're skipping their land drop for the turn. They should play a land first (like Breeding Pool untapped paying 2 life, or Starting Town) and then cast Earthen Ally.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Earthen Ally from hand without first playing a land for turn 3.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (e.g., Breeding Pool or Starting Town) to ensure the land drop isn't missed, then cast Earthen Ally. Playing the land first loses nothing and ensures maximum mana development.

annotations.description: Evoking Wistfulness for card filtering (draw 2, discard 1) uses the entire turn's mana when stronger development plays were available. Playing Gloomlake Verge first would give 3 lands, enabling Overlord of the Balemurk for impending cost {1}{B} which starts a powerful threat ticking down, or Formidable Speaker {2}{G} which provides a body and creature tutor.
annotations.actionTaken: Evoked Wistfulness for {G/U}{G/U}, spending all available mana on card filtering (draw 2, discard 1) with no board development.
annotations.betterLine: Play Gloomlake Verge, then cast Overlord of the Balemurk for impending {1}{B}, developing a powerful threat while keeping cards in hand for future turns.

annotations.description: Discarding Bringer of the Last Gift to Wistfulness's draw-discard trigger. Bringer is a powerful reanimation target that returns all creatures from graveyards when cast, and with Overlord of the Balemurk's mill/reanimate ability available, having Bringer in the graveyard could be useful. However, the player has two Overlord of the Balemurk in hand which can mill and return creatures, so putting Bringer in the graveyard could actually be part of a plan to reanimate it later. The alternative consideration is discarding one of the duplicate Formidable Speakers or duplicate Gloomlake Verges, which are less impactful cards. Discarding a land (Gloomlake Verge) when you only have 2 lands in play and need to ramp to cast expensive threats like Overlord or Ardyn seems wrong. Discarding a duplicate Formidable Speaker might preserve more options since Bringer of the Last Gift is a unique and powerful effect. That said, Bringer costs 8 mana and is very far from being castable, and Overlord can potentially return it from the graveyard, so this discard has some logic to it.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Bringer of the Last Gift to Wistfulness's draw-discard trigger
annotations.betterLine: Discarding a duplicate Formidable Speaker would preserve the unique powerful Bringer while still keeping one copy of the tutor creature. However, the Bringer discard is defensible if planning to use Overlord of the Balemurk to return it from the graveyard later.

annotations.description: With 4 lands available (producing G, U, B), the player could have cast both Formidable Speaker (2G = 3 mana) and Overlord of the Balemurk for its Impending cost (1B = 2 mana). Wait - that's 5 mana total with only 4 lands. However, Formidable Speaker costs 2G (3 mana) and uses most of the mana, leaving only 1 mana. Overlord impending costs 1B (2 mana). So actually they can't cast both. The real question is whether Formidable Speaker (getting a body + creature tutor) would have been better than Overlord impending. Formidable Speaker tutors a key creature while providing a 2/4 body, which is likely more impactful at this stage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk (likely for impending 1B cost) to mill 4 and potentially recur from graveyard
annotations.betterLine: Cast Formidable Speaker for 2G, discarding a less useful card (like a second Overlord) to tutor for a key creature like Bringer of the Last Gift, providing both a body and card selection

annotations.description: With only 4 lands producing at most GGUB (Breeding Pool, Hedge Maze, 2x Gloomlake Verge), casting Overlord of the Balemurk for its full cost of {3}{B}{B} requires all 4 lands and is tight on mana. More importantly, casting it for Impending {1}{B} costs only 2 mana, leaving 2 mana open for Spell Snare (which is in hand). The Impending version still triggers the mill-4 + return creature ETB effect immediately, which is extremely valuable since there's a Bringer of the Last Gift and Wistfulness already in the graveyard. The 5-turn clock to become a creature is acceptable since the opponent has minimal board presence (just lands). By paying full cost, Hype taps out completely, leaving no mana for Spell Snare and gaining only the immediate 5/5 body — which isn't under pressure to need. The Impending cost would have been far more efficient, preserving interaction.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for full cost {3}{B}{B}, tapping all 4 lands
annotations.betterLine: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for Impending cost {1}{B}, leaving 2 mana open for Spell Snare or other interaction. The ETB mill trigger still fires, and the opponent's minimal board means there's no urgency for the 5/5 body.

annotations.description: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for Impending instead of Formidable Speaker. The Overlord won't be a creature for 5 turns, while Formidable Speaker provides an immediate 2/4 body, a creature tutor (discard to search), and leaves 1 mana open for Spell Snare against opponent's 2-drops. With only 4 lands and needing to ramp toward expensive threats like Ardyn or Bringer, the tutor is more impactful than milling 4.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for Impending cost {1}{B}, getting mill 4 + graveyard recursion but no creature for 5 turns.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Formidable Speaker for {2}{G}, getting an immediate 2/4 creature, tutoring for a key card (like a land enabler or threat), and leaving 1 mana open for Spell Snare to protect against opponent's plays.

annotations.description: GPT5n Undrdog played Great Divide Guide (a creature) before combat rather than playing a land first. They have multiple untapped lands in hand (Floodfarm Verge, Breeding Pool, Starting Town) and only 2 lands on board. Additionally, casting a creature before combat when holding Allies at Last (a combat trick) is slightly suboptimal sequencing — playing the creature pre-combat telegraphs information. More importantly, with only 2 lands on the battlefield, they should have played a land first to have 3 mana available, which would allow casting Great Divide Guide more efficiently or keeping mana open for other plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Great Divide Guide before playing a land drop for the turn.

annotations.description: With 4 lands on board and the postcombat main phase, Grk41F Hype should cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost of {1}{B} (2 mana) rather than just playing a tapped land. The Overlord's impending mode starts the countdown and triggers mill 4 + recursion on entry, which would retrieve a powerful creature like Bringer of the Last Gift, Wistfulness, or Deceit from the graveyard. Playing Underground Mortuary tapped means no mana was used this turn. They could have played the land AND cast Overlord for impending cost, or at minimum cast the Overlord with available mana. However, looking more carefully: they have Breeding Pool (G/U), Hedge Maze (tapped - entered this turn? No, it entered turn 3), Gloomlake Verge x2 (U, or B if controlling Island/Swamp). Breeding Pool is an Island, so Gloomlake Verge can tap for B. They have access to at least 1B from Gloomlake Verge + Gloomlake Verge, which is exactly {1}{B} for Overlord's impending cost. They could also cast Formidable Speaker for {2}{G} using Breeding Pool for G + two other lands. Playing just a tapped land and passing with 4 mana available wastes the turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Underground Mortuary (enters tapped) as the only action, leaving 4 lands untapped and unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost {1}{B} using two Gloomlake Verges (one for {B}, one for {C} via Breeding Pool), triggering mill 4 and potential graveyard recursion, then play Underground Mortuary. Alternatively, cast Formidable Speaker for {2}{G} to tutor a creature.

annotations.description: Casting Overlord of the Balemurk for full cost {3}{B}{B} uses all 5 mana this turn to get an immediate 5/5 with ETB mill 4 + recursion. However, casting it for Impending {1}{B} would only cost 2 mana, leaving 3 mana open - critically leaving up mana for Spell Snare (which costs {U}) to protect against opponent's 2-mana plays. The opponent is at only 2 lands and likely deploying cheap threats. While getting an immediate 5/5 body with ETB is powerful, especially against an opponent with an empty board, the Impending cost would let Grk41F hold up Spell Snare and still develop the Overlord (arriving as a creature in 5 turns). Additionally, with Bringer of the Last Gift in the graveyard, the Overlord's ETB mill could find more creatures but the recursion target (Bringer) is already known. The immediate pressure of a 5/5 against an opponent with no board is strong, but leaving up interaction while still developing is arguably better tempo since the opponent can't block anyway and won't be under lethal pressure immediately.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Overlord of the Balemurk for Impending {1}{B}, leaving 3 mana open including blue for Spell Snare to counter opponent's 2-mana plays while still developing the enchantment that becomes a 5/5 in 5 turns

annotations.description: With 5 lands available (Breeding Pool, Hedge Maze, Gloomlake Verge x2, Underground Mortuary) and Formidable Speaker already on board, casting Overlord of the Balemurk for full cost {3}{B}{B} uses all 5 mana this turn. The ETB mills 4 and returns a creature/planeswalker from graveyard (likely Bringer of the Last Gift or Deceit). However, casting for impending {1}{B} would only cost 2 mana, leaving 3 mana open for other plays - potentially casting a second Formidable Speaker (2G) this turn for additional value (tutor effect + board presence). The Overlord as a 5/5 creature is nice but the opponent has no board presence (just 2 lands), so there's no urgency for an immediate 5/5 body. The impending version still provides the enchantment's mill/recursion trigger every end step when time counters are removed, and the ETB trigger fires when it enters (even as impending). Actually, wait - with impending, it enters as a non-creature enchantment and the ETB 'whenever this permanent enters' trigger still fires, giving the mill 4 + recursion immediately. So impending gives you the same ETB value while saving 3 mana. The tradeoff is waiting 5 turns for the creature body, but with no opposing pressure at 18 life, that's very manageable. Casting for full cost when you could get the same ETB and have 3 mana for Formidable Speaker's tutor is likely suboptimal.

annotations.description: Allies at Last allows up to two creatures to each deal damage equal to their power to a target opponent's creature. GPT5n Undrdog chose to target Formidable Speaker (a 2/4) instead of a much more threatening creature. Overlord of the Balemurk is a 5/5 that mills and recurs creatures from the graveyard - it's the primary engine generating card advantage and board presence. Harvester of Misery is a 5/4 with menace that gave -2/-2 on ETB. At 5 life, removing the biggest threat is critical. Without knowing exactly which creatures GPT5n controlled to deal damage, targeting the 2/4 Formidable Speaker over the 5/5 Overlord or 5/4 Harvester wastes the removal spell on the least threatening creature on the opponent's board.

annotations.description: Grk41F Hype has Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5), Harvester of Misery (5/4), and Formidable Speaker (2/4) on the battlefield against an opponent at 5 life with no creatures. Any combination of attackers totaling 5+ power would be lethal. Overlord alone (5 power) is lethal. Harvester alone (5 power) is lethal. Yet the combat phase passed without declaring any attackers, allowing the opponent to survive at 5 life and take another turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to use any instants/abilities during combat and passed without attacking, giving the opponent another turn at 5 life.

annotations.description: Allies at Last allows up to two creatures you control to each deal damage equal to their power to a target creature an opponent controls. GPT5n Undrdog has no creatures on the battlefield (only lands), so Allies at Last has no valid creatures to assign as damage sources. The spell accomplishes nothing regardless of which opponent's creature is targeted. However, the choice of Formidable Speaker (a 2/4) over either Overlord of the Balemurk (5/5) or Harvester of Misery (5/4) is terrible targeting even if they had creatures. Formidable Speaker is the least threatening creature on the opponent's board compared to the 5/5 Overlord (which mills and recurs cards) and the 5/4 Harvester of Misery (which gave -2/-2 to all other creatures). Targeting a real threat like Overlord of the Balemurk or Harvester of Misery would have been correct if the spell could actually deal damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Formidable Speaker with Allies at Last, the least threatening creature on the opponent's board.
annotations.betterLine: Target Overlord of the Balemurk or Harvester of Misery, as these are the primary threats. Though with no creatures on board, the spell likely does nothing regardless - the card may have been uncastable or wasted.

The Overlord is a 5/5 that mills and recurs creatures every turn, and the Harvester is a 5/4 with menace and an ETB -2/-2 effect. At 5 life, removing a 5/5 or 5/4 attacker is critical for survival, while the 2/4 Formidable Speaker poses minimal combat threat.
